linkedin.title: Personalised news is currently broken because it prioritises engagement over understanding.
linkedin.body:
For years, algorithms have fed us what they think we want to click on. The result is a cycle of outrage and shallow headlines that leave us feeling less informed, not more. We think the next phase of news needs to be different.

At Headlinne, we are building a roadmap that focuses on utility and depth. Instead of just showing you more of what you already read, we want to build tools that help you connect the dots between complex stories. The goal is to save you time while actually increasing your knowledge.

True personalisation isn't about profiling your habits to keep you scrolling longer. It is about respecting your time by filtering out the noise and delivering the information that matters to your life. We are moving away from the black box approach and toward a model where you have more control over what you see and why you see it.

slides.headline: Smoke rises near Riyadh airport after Houthi attack
slides.subtitle: The first public alerts for Riyadh since July

slides.explanation: While specific casualty numbers remain unconfirmed, the visible smoke near a major international airport marks a significant escalation in the ongoing conflict.

slides.headline: This is the first Riyadh alert since July
slides.explanation: The Houthis claim they used both missiles and drones to target what they described as sensitive sites in the capital.
We verified these reports across four independent news outlets, including the BBC and Al Jazeera, to ensure the facts are accurate.

slides.subtitle: Read the full breakdown on Headlinne.

instagram.caption:
Thick black smoke was captured rising above the airport in Riyadh earlier today.

The Houthis, an Iran-backed group, have claimed responsibility for the attack, stating they targeted sensitive locations with a mix of missiles and drones.

This marks the first time authorities have issued alerts for the Saudi capital since tensions escalated this past July. The situation is still developing as local officials assess the damage.

story.title: Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport as Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital
story.summary: Authorities issued warnings for city in first such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July Yemen’s Houthis said they attacked “sensitive” sites in the Saudi capital with missiles and drones, hours after flames and a large plume of black smoke were seen rising above Riyadh airport on Saturday. The Saudi government sent air raid alerts to citizens by phone overnight warning of aerial attacks, marking the first time the government has issued such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with the Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July. story_card.headline: Firefox 156 arrives amid a sea of alternatives
story_card.standfirst: The browser landscape is expanding as users increasingly turn to custom forks of Firefox.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Firefox 156 is here, but it is sharing the stage with a growing number of alternative versions.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Over time, many users became dissatisfied with Mozilla. They created their own spin-off browsers.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Browsers like Waterfox, LibreWolf, and Pale Moon show that people want more control and choice.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: See if these niche browsers can keep up with the rapid update pace of the main Firefox release.

story_card.caption:
Firefox 156 has launched, but many users are choosing to stick with browser forks like LibreWolf and Waterfox.

The open-source nature of Firefox allows developers to create custom versions tailored to specific needs. These forks often appeal to users looking for different privacy settings or interface tweaks that the official browser does not offer. It highlights a fragmented but active community of Mozilla dissenters.
